subject.title: Generalize post-timeout compaction completion reconciliation across session state

question: Should successful compaction completion become the authoritative reconciliation boundary for all compaction-derived session state, and which fields should that boundary own beyond `compactionCount`?
rationale: Source inspection confirms the current implementation is intentionally count-only while several session consumers read related but separate state; choosing the permanent ownership boundary is product/architecture judgment, not a safe automatic repair.

options.title: Promote The Existing Event Boundary
options.body: Make the successful compaction-end path own monotonic updates for count, fresh token snapshot, session rotation metadata, and other clearly compaction-derived fields, with focused late-signal tests.

options.title: Keep Count-Only Reconciliation
options.body: Leave the shipped narrow repair as-is and require separate issues for each remaining stale state surface before changing more session state.

options.title: Wait For Live Repro
options.body: Keep the issue open but block implementation until a current-main late-success case proves which additional user-visible fields diverge.

recommendation.title: Promote The Existing Event Boundary
recommendation.body: Make the successful compaction-end path own monotonic updates for count, fresh token snapshot, session rotation metadata, and other clearly compaction-derived fields, with focused late-signal tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work on session totals and stale/fresh state makes this the best available owner signal for deciding which non-counter fields belong in the reconciliation boundary.
